findings.title: Reopened row still restarts the run on click
findings.problem: The isReopenOf branch of onPrompt un-collapses an answered row and renders a fresh control inside it, but never removes the onclick, keydown handler, 'revisit' class or role set by makeRevisitable (lines 443-455). onPrompt has also just called setRevisitOpen(true), so revisit() passes its guard. A click on the reopened input or option cards, or Space or Enter in the input, bubbles to the row and calls restart(replayPrefix(rowId)). The row's keydown handler also calls preventDefault on Space, so a space cannot be typed into the reopened input.
findings.impact: After a validation rejection (e.g. a bad CodeMie URL), clicking into the input to correct it cancels the live setup process and replays from the start. The user loses the correction and the reopened prompt.
findings.recommendation: On reopen, make the row non-revisitable. Clear row.onclick and the 'revisit' class, remove role and tabIndex, and keep the keydown listener as a named function so it can be removed. Alternatively, have the handlers ignore events whose target is inside .prompt-control or while the row is not collapsed, and call makeRevisitable only once. Add a test that clicking inside a reopened input does not call cancelSetup.
